title: Risk-weighted legacy-contract mixed league 65k pilot
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: The smoke-validated public-risk source-margin objective can retain Standard10 high-leverage greedy boundaries while the previously promising mixed FIFO league accumulates enough fresh self-play/procedural experience to create a stronger transferable frozen policy.
material_change: Scale the risk-weighted treatment from 8k to 65,536 target physical hands with fresh seeds/deals; retain the prior 65k legacy-contract mixed-league architecture, low LR, source KL, opponent mixture, FIFO cadence, and trainable tensor scope while adding source-greedy margin coefficient 0.1 and max public-risk weight 4 at a 0.15 pot/effective-stack threshold.
baseline: Prior unweighted 69,288-hand mixed league iter16 passed fresh internal replication at +14.9376 bb/100 adjusted CI[2.3311,27.5441] but failed fresh20k Slumbot at -37.1617 CI[-58.9246,-15.3988]. Its outcome-blind audit found amplified high-risk drift. The matched 8k risk smoke reduced >=30bb TV 0.01039->0.00946, disagreement 0.976%->0.878%, and margin deficit 0.001628->0.001379; this is mechanism, not strength evidence.

notes: Before outcomes: audit exact session and tensor scope; evaluate iter4/8/12/16 on one common 50k outcome-blind source-state set including >=30bb strata. Then run a fresh common-randomness four-anchor internal panel. No Slumbot unless a frozen archive passes a preregistered multiplicity-aware lower-bound gate, >=3/4 positive anchors, both seats nonnegative, and raw evidence audit.
Training completed normally at 69,236 physical hands, 65,810 transition-bearing hands, iteration 16. Frozen archives and evidence are now under audit; no external hands were spent.

Fresh common-state endpoint comparison falsified scaled high-risk improvement: despite lower overall drift, risk-weighted iter16 is worse than prior unweighted iter16 on every >=30bb preservation metric. Complete the preregistered archive-level strength panel before deciding whether any earlier archive is useful.

Fresh 81,920-hand internal panel produced no eligible archive. Iter16 was strongest at +17.5837 bb/100 pooled, 3/4 positive anchors and both seat points positive, but its four-comparison adjusted lower bound was -3.3150; no Slumbot is authorized.

result.summary: The risk-weighted mixed league completed 69,236 audited physical hands and produced four frozen archives. All archives passed broad source-preservation gates, but scaled iter16 worsened >=30bb source preservation versus the prior unweighted iter16 and no archive passed the fresh 81,920-hand internal promotion gate.
result.conclusion: Risk weighting improved aggregate iter16 source drift relative to the prior unweighted pilot (mean TV about 0.0183 vs 0.0241; disagreement 2.23% vs 3.02% on one fresh comparison) but did not preserve the intended high-leverage states at scale: >=30bb TV rose by 0.00757, disagreement by 1.04 percentage points, and margin deficit by 0.00495. Iter16 had a promising internal +17.5837 bb/100 point with 3/4 anchors and both seat points positive, but adjusted lower bound -3.3150 failed. The fixed release threshold likely lets large raw high-pot advantages release protection disproportionately; this is a hypothesis for a new mechanism test, not a retrospective explanation treated as fact.
result.next_step: Implement a default-off option that scales the source-margin release threshold by the same public risk weight, so high-pot boundaries require proportionally stronger advantage evidence to release. First run a small matched smoke measuring released/violation rows and common-state >=30bb drift; do not scale or spend Slumbot unless the direct high-risk mechanism improves without blocking all reward-supported release.
